highlight.title: Cloud Run Gets GPU Support & Multi-Region Deployments
highlight.summary: <cite index="5-7">NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs are now available on Cloud Run</cite> for high-performance AI inference. <cite index="1-8">Multi-region service deployment is now possible from a single gcloud CLI command</cite>, and <cite index="1-9">service-level minimum instances are now generally available</cite> for better cold-start control.

resources.title: Cloud Run Pricing Guide 2025: Cost Optimization Strategies
resources.why_now: <cite index="12-26,12-27">Tuning concurrency is a key cost optimization lever in 2025</cite>, and <cite index="15-5,15-6">Compute Flex CUDs now provide broader service coverage and higher discount rates than Cloud Run-specific CUDs</cite>.

resources.title: Google Secret Manager Complete Tutorial 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="21-22">No JSON key files should touch production GKE clusters in 2026</cite> - the guide shows proper Workload Identity integration patterns. <cite index="21-24,21-25">The free tier covers six active versions and 10,000 access operations monthly</cite>, making it cost-effective for most workloads.

resources.title: Cloud Native Architecture Patterns 2026 Guide
resources.why_now: <cite index="38-1">AI-assisted pattern selection and enhanced observability integration with OpenTelemetry</cite> are key 2026 trends. <cite index="37-6,37-7">Event-driven systems will be default for high-scale applications by 2026</cite>, making these patterns essential for modern GCP deployments.

resources.title: GCP Cost Optimization for Data-Heavy Applications 2025
resources.why_now: <cite index="13-21,13-22">GKE Autopilot charges by vCPU-seconds containers request, not actual usage</cite>, and <cite index="13-22,13-23">GKE 2025 exposes cost-optimization metrics in Cloud Monitoring for right-sizing workloads</cite>.

claude_take: GCP's 2026 direction is clear: serverless gets serious GPU power while cost optimization becomes more sophisticated through automated rightsizing and flexible CUDs. The shift to event-driven architectures isn't just trendy—it's becoming table stakes for any serious cloud application, especially with improved Secret Manager and IAM patterns making security seamless.
